answer: A credit-network protocol curbs Sybil attacks by routing reputation through bilateral trust channels authenticated with compact falcon signatures. Max-flow bottlenecks prevent adversaries from inflating influence via an isolated knoll of collusive nodes, while time-decay ensures no inactive identity persists as a trusted relic. An attacker incurs the verifiable, scarce cost of bonding liquid capital across honest peers per identity. However, this restricts entry for honest, unvouched agents.
